title: Gateway H20: the per-frame workspace ownership check gives upstream's exact answer at a fraction of the cost, and still refuses another subuser's workspace
steps: S1: Compare H20 with upstream's predicate over aliases, symlinks, missing and dangling folders, roles and shared grants; count rows reads and filesystem calls on the dev host's shape (117 rows, 87 missing folders).
S2: Through the real gateway, a seat granted a folder another subuser registered lists it and opens a session there.
expect: S1: every answer equals upstream's; one rows read per check, realpath only per existing folder; faster than upstream's predicate.
S2: the folder is not listed and session creation is refused with 403, nothing sent to dsh.
evidence: Dev profile 25/10/2026: workspaceOwnedByAnotherSubuser was 49% of gateway samples; on dev's real rows H20 gave 702/702 identical answers, 5.79 ms -> 1.34 ms per check
fence: Unit test against upstream's predicate rebuilt from its exported helpers, plus a gateway harness test through H20

tests: H20: the same answer as upstream
🔒 H20: a workspace another subuser owns is still refused
H20: per check, one read of the rows
🔒 H20: another seat granted that folder
🔒 H20: and the other seat is refused
